# QS-CFW-2573-68 - Quality specification - axle hub CFW-2573-68 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-2573-68  
Related documents: none

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufacturing, inspection, and disposition of axle hub CFW-2573-68 (CFW-2573-68) produced from material grade 4140 at Plant P3. It defines acceptance criteria for metallurgical and dimensional characteristics that directly affect fit, form, and function in downstream assembly and service. The intent is to provide clear, enforceable criteria for production, in-process control, final inspection, and nonconformance handling to minimize scrap and rework while protecting safety and reliability.

Background and rationale
- Axle hubs carry loads transmitted through bearings and fasteners; their hardness and bore geometry are critical to maintain interference fits and bearing life. The hardness range 25-31 HRC is selected to balance toughness and wear resistance for 4140 material in this application. The bore diameter tolerance ±0.03 mm ensures consistent fit with mating shafts and bearings without excessive rework. The maximum forging weight 97.2 kg establishes limits for forging operations, handling equipment, and heat treatment load capacity.
- These parameters were derived from service requirements and manufacturing capability assessments. Hardness outside the specified range can indicate improper quench or temper conditions or decarburization. Bore out of tolerance can cause assembly interference or looseness; uncontrolled forging weight can exceed press or furnace capacity and compromise process control.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the controlled characteristics, acceptance criteria, and responsible function for verification.

| Characteristic | Acceptance criteria | Responsible function |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 as specified on purchase order and material certificate | Purchasing / Receiving |
| Hardness (throughout critical cross section) | 25-31 HRC | Heat treat / Quality |
| Bore diameter | Within drawing nominal plus or minus ±0.03 mm | Machining / Quality |
| Surface condition | Free of defects that affect function; no visible cracks or severe laps | Machining / Quality |
| Forging weight (as-delivered) | Not to exceed maximum forging weight 97.2 kg | Forging / Production |
| Final visual and functional check | Conforms to drawing and assembly requirements | Quality / Assembly |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Verify material certificate matches procurement specification and that material grade is 4140. Record the certificate reference in the job lot file.
  - Confirm forging gross mass is not above maximum forging weight 97.2 kg by cross reference to the forging work order and handling documentation. If forging mass is unspecified on the work order, use scale ticket supplied by forging operations and attach to the lot record.
- In-process inspection
  - Hardness control: perform hardness verification on representative locations identified in the inspection plan. Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Measurements must confirm hardness within 25-31 HRC across the critical cross section. Document all readings in the heat treat record. If readings trend toward the limits, notify heat treat process owner to evaluate process settings and quench/temper procedure.
  - Bore verification: measure bore diameter using the measurement method specified on the drawing or inspection plan. Measurements must be within ±0.03 mm of the nominal drawing diameter. Record measurements on the dimensional inspection sheet and attach to the lot passport.
  - Surface and visual inspection: inspect for forging laps, cracks, inclusions, scale, and other defects prior to machining. Critical defects require containment and escalation to quality engineering.
- Final inspection
  - Verify that all hardness values recorded during heat treat are within 25-31 HRC and that all bore measurements are within ±0.03 mm. Confirm surface condition and that no nonconformances remain open. Complete final inspection checklist and file with process records.
- Calibration and equipment
  - Ensure hardness tester and bore measuring equipment are within valid calibration. Calibration certificates must be referenced in the inspection record. If an instrument is found out of calibration, quarantined lot measurements must be re-established with a calibrated instrument and documented.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and containment
  - Any part or lot that fails to meet hardness criteria 25-31 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.03 mm, or exceeds maximum forging weight 97.2 kg shall be identified, segregated, and tagged as nonconforming. Segregation must prevent inadvertent use.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - Quality shall evaluate the root cause and propose a disposition: rework, repair, use-as-is with acceptance by engineering, or scrap. Evaluation shall include review of process data from forging, heat treat, and machining.
  - Rework examples: if bore is marginally out of tolerance and material remains within drawing allowance, machining to an alternate size with appropriate mating parts or use of approved oversize bearing may be considered only after engineering approval and with traceability recorded. If hardness is out of range due to reversible processing, reheat and temper or re-quench may be considered only if metallurgical assessment supports the action and records are maintained.
  - Scrap: parts that exhibit critical defects such as through-thickness cracks, excessive decarburization, or damage incompatible with repair shall be scrapped and documented.
- Records and traceability
  - For every nonconformance, maintain a nonconformance report in the lot file that includes part identification, time and source of discovery, measured deviation from requirement, immediate containment action, root cause analysis summary, disposition decision, and corrective actions. Attach relevant process data: heat treat records, hardness readings, bore measurement sheets, forging weight documentation, and calibration certificates.
  - Retain records in the job lot file and the quality management system in accordance with company retention rules.
- Corrective action and prevention
  - If nonconformances repeat or indicate systemic process issues, initiate corrective action. The corrective action shall include containment verification, root cause analysis, process parameter review, training if required, and monitoring to confirm effectiveness. Quality shall track corrective actions until closure and include evidence demonstrating that risk of recurrence has been reduced.

Examples and notes
- Example situations are provided for clarity. If a lot exhibits hardness values just outside 25-31 HRC at the outer surface but passes internal measurements, engineering metallurgical evaluation is required before disposition. If a single part bore measurement exceeds ±0.03 mm while the remainder of the lot is within tolerance, evaluate whether machining recovery is feasible and document the decision and method.
- Maintain clear linkage between forging batch, heat treat load, machining batch, and final lot to ensure traceability from forging through final inspection.

Records to keep
- Material certificate for 4140
- Forging weight documentation referencing maximum forging weight 97.2 kg
- Heat treat records with hardness readings showing 25-31 HRC
- Dimensional inspection sheets showing bore measurements within ±0.03 mm
- Calibration certificates for measurement equipment
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation

End of specification.
